name: Landline
description:
Landline — your iPhone's calls, messages and notifications on the GNOME desktop.

A quiet dot in the top bar when the iPhone is linked over Bluetooth. When something arrives the dot grows into a pill: read and answer an SMS or iMessage from a small card, answer or decline a call and choose whether its sound plays on the computer or on the iPhone. Notifications of the other iPhone apps appear in the GNOME notification list. The menu also shows the battery level, recent calls, and can switch on the iPhone's Personal Hotspot connection. Nothing is installed on the iPhone and no account or cloud service is involved.

USES A SEPARATE ENGINE. The extension is only the interface. The Bluetooth work is done by a small background service, the Landline engine, which is not part of this extension's package. Phone Settings › Engine installs it in one click, on your request: it downloads the engine release this version of the extension was made for from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 against the value written in the extension, unpacks it into ~/.local/lib/landline/engine and starts it as a systemd user service. Instructions and the manual way: https://github.com/d101c/landline#install
Without the engine the extension shows "Landline needs its engine" and does nothing else.

What the extension does on your system:
- Processes it starts: "systemctl --user start landline-engine.service" once when the engine does not answer; "systemctl --user restart landline-engine.service" when you click "Fix It"; and the read-only "status" command of the engine's setup helper (landline-setup, when installed), to know whether the Bluetooth settings are in place.
- Installing the engine (Phone Settings › Engine, preferences window only, on a click): download with libsoup, unpacking with libgnome-autoar, files written in ~/.cache/landline, ~/.local/lib/landline and ~/.config/systemd/user (the user service and a drop-in that restarts BlueZ's obexd), and systemd's D-Bus API (reload, enable, restart, stop, disable). No process is started for this. The previous engine is kept for "Use Previous Engine". "Uninstall the Engine…" removes all of it.
- Administrator password: only on systems where a Bluetooth setting required by iPhones is missing (BlueZ older than 5.88 needs its experimental mode; some systems disable L2CAP ERTM). The setup dialog then offers to change it ("pkexec /usr/local/libexec/landline/landline-setup apply"), and the "Undo" button of Phone Settings puts it back ("pkexec /usr/local/libexec/landline/landline-setup revert"). In both cases the password window is the system's own (pkexec), and it is only ever used on the setup helper that the engine's installer placed in that root-owned directory, after checking that the file belongs to root and that nobody else can write it. If that helper is not installed yet, the setup dialog shows the commands to run yourself; Phone Settings › Engine can install it instead, after an engine install, with "pkexec /bin/sh -c '<script>'": a fixed script written in the extension that copies landline-setup and its helper out of the home folder into a new root-owned directory, checks the SHA-256 of the copies against values written in the script itself, and only then runs the root copy ("apply"), which installs itself in /usr/local/libexec/landline. A file the user can change is never run as root. Cancelling the password window changes nothing.
- Clipboard: the "Copy Commands" buttons (setup dialog, Phone Settings › Engine) write those commands to the clipboard when you click them. The extension never reads the clipboard.
- Official apps: on a notification of Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram, Teams, Discord, Slack or Messenger, "Open in …" opens the official app installed on this computer (found through the desktop's own list of apps and link handlers, cached), or the service's official web client, on your click; for WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal on the sender's conversation when their phone number is known for sure (web.whatsapp.com, tg:, sgnl:). Only official apps and web clients are ever offered. When the official app is missing, the card says so once and links to its official download page; "Suggest official apps" in Phone Settings turns that off.
- Phone links (off by default): "Use Landline for phone links" in Phone Settings writes ~/.local/share/applications/landline-phone-links.desktop and makes it the default for tel: and callto: links, asking first when another app has them. When no app on the computer opens these links, the top bar menu offers the same option once ("Use Landline" / "Not Now"); it is never offered again, and never when another app has them; turned off, the file is removed and the previous default is put back. A clicked link runs "gdbus call" on an object the extension exports on the Shell's session bus connection while the option is on; the top bar then asks "Call …?" before anything is dialled. With the extension disabled, the call fails at once and nothing happens.
- Network: the engine download from github.com described above, when you click Install or Update. App icons: to show the real icon of an iPhone app next to its notifications, the app's identifier (like net.whatsapp.WhatsApp) and the country of your locale are sent to Apple's public App Store lookup (itunes.apple.com), once per app, and the icon is then downloaded from Apple's image server (mzstatic.com) and kept in ~/.cache/landline/app-icons. Nothing of the notification itself is sent. Phone Settings › "Show app icons" turns this off (on by default). "Use iPhone's Internet Connection" asks NetworkManager to turn the iPhone's existing Bluetooth profile on or off.
- No telemetry.

Limits:
- iPhone only. Text replies work for SMS and iMessage; for other apps the extension shows the notification and can open the app, but cannot send a reply itself.
- Photos and other attachments are not shown, group conversations cannot be started from the computer.
- The extension is inactive on the lock screen.
- Tested on GNOME 51 with BlueZ 5.87 and PipeWire.

The engine is derived from Tether by Zack Bartel (MIT licence): https://github.com/zackb/tether
